Marinated Olives with Pomegranate and Walnuts

Served at: Yalda Night

Serves 6-8Prep 15 min

This vibrant dish is a delightful addition to the Yalda Night (Shab-e Yalda) spread, celebrating the winter solstice and the longest night of the year. Pomegranates are a quintessential symbol of Yalda, representing life and rebirth, and when combined with briny olives and crunchy walnuts, they create a festive and flavorful appetizer that perfectly complements the traditional fruits and nuts of the occasion.

Ingredients

  • 2 cups (about 300g) mixed pitted olives, such as Kalamata and Castelvetrano
  • 1/2 cup (75g) pomegranate arils (from about 1/2 a large pomegranate)
  • 1/2 cup (60g) walnuts, roughly chopped
  • 1/4 cup (60ml) fresh pomegranate juice
  • 2 tablespoons (30ml) extra virgin olive oil
  • 1 tablespoon (15ml) fresh lemon juice
  • 2 cloves garlic, minced
  • 2 tablespoons fresh mint, finely chopped
  • 1 tablespoon fresh parsley, finely chopped
  • 1/4 teaspoon black pepper, freshly ground
  • Pinch of sea salt (optional, depending on olive saltiness)

Method

  1. Rinse the pitted olives gently under cold water and pat them dry with a paper towel. Place them in a medium-sized mixing bowl.
  2. Add the pomegranate arils and chopped walnuts to the bowl with the olives.
  3. In a small separate bowl, whisk together the pomegranate juice, olive oil, lemon juice, minced garlic, chopped mint, chopped parsley, and black pepper.
  4. Pour the dressing over the olive mixture. Gently toss all ingredients together until everything is well coated.
  5. Taste and add a pinch of sea salt if needed, keeping in mind that olives are already quite salty.
  6. Cover the bowl and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes to allow the flavors to meld. For best results, marinate for 2-4 hours.
  7. Before serving, give the mixture another gentle stir and serve chilled or at room temperature.

Tips

  • For an extra layer of flavor, lightly toast the walnuts in a dry skillet for a few minutes until fragrant before chopping.
  • A touch of orange zest can be added to the marinade for a brighter, citrusy note.
  • This dish can be prepared a day in advance; the flavors will deepen beautifully overnight in the refrigerator.
